why: After seeing the screens, readers want to know what the project can actually do and how much of it is finished. A short checklist lets them tell at a glance.
question: What can it do, and what is already built?
who: Required for web apps, portfolios and backend APIs

parts.heading: Completed features
parts.text: Use - [x] checkboxes, one user-facing action per line—such as "Browse the menu and prices by category"—and keep it to three to eight items.
parts.emphasis: Write what a user can do, not implementation details like "State management with Pinia".

parts.heading: Unfinished features
parts.text: Mark items that are not finished yet with - [ ] and add "(in progress)". Being upfront about what is unfinished builds more trust than pretending everything is done.

lines.text: [[This system lets customers browse the menu, add items]]
[[to the cart, and place orders on their phone.]]

notes.title: Written as a paragraph
notes.text: Use a one-item-per-line checklist so readers can scan.

notes.title: Lists tech as features
notes.text: Describe what users can do; put tools under Tech Stack.

notes.title: Leftover template text
notes.text: Replace unfinished "..." lines with real items or delete them.

lines: - [x] Browse the menu and prices by category
- [x] Add items to the cart and change quantities
- [x] Pick a pickup time and submit the order

tip.title: Start each item with a verb from the user's point of view
paragraphs: Try reading each line after "A user can…": "browse the menu by category" and "pick a pickup time and submit the order" fit naturally, while "responsive layout" or "component architecture" do not.
Keep unfinished items to one or two things you genuinely plan to build next, not a long wish list.

types.web-app: List the actions customers or admins can perform on the screens.
types.course-example: Use "## Learning Objectives" and "## Course Unit" instead, stating what students will learn and which lesson it belongs to.
types.portfolio: Add a "## My Role" section right below to state what you built in a team project, or that you built the whole project solo.
types.backend-api: List the main capabilities or endpoint groups here, and leave full request schemas to the API documentation.
